newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy not yet certain of meeting EMU goal - Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italy not yet certain of meeting EMU goal - Ciampi.

text.p: Italy is not yet certain to meet its deficit goal for 1997, with the autumn months posing a potential threat to state accounts, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in a newspaper interview.

Italy has pledged to cut its deficit to three percent of gross domestic product this year from 6.7 percent in 1996, to meet a key criteria laid down in the Maastricht Treaty for countries wishing to join the single European currency.
But Ciampi said that despite a strong start to the year, Italy was not home and dry.
"We're not safe yet because the last months of the year involve large flows of funds, so there could still be surprises," Ciampi told financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore.
"The forecast today is that we should close the year with a deficit which will be around half that of 1996," he said.

"This was our aim and translated in terms of the public administration deficit would be three percent (of GDP)," he added. The public administration deficit is the figure quoted by the Maastricht Treaty.
Italy recorded a state sector deficit of 29.75 trillion lire in the first seven months of 1997 against 63.6 trillion lire in the same period last year.
"In August, the situation should improve still further," Ciampi said. "Last year the deficit (in August) was 8.4 trillion lire and this year it should be much less.
"It's clear that September, October and November will not present changes of a similar dimension. In any case we should have a good recovery in December," he added.
Ciampi's caution on the deficit outlook for the autumn was echoed by Giorgio Macciotta, undersecretary at the Treasury. However, Macciotta thought November might see accounts improve.

"There could be some problem in September and October, which are risky months. In November self-taxation revenue arrives which will bring the three percent level close to hand," Macciotta was quoted as saying by La Stampa newspaper. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
